brief.headline: Aluminium set a second straight higher official - cash $3,271.00, 3M $3,236.50, stock a 25th-consecutive-draw century low of 260,900 t - but this time it rose WITH the geopolitical tape rather than against it, because the 48-hour-old de-escalation story collapsed: Tehran denied talks, Washington called it duplicity, another ship was struck in Hormuz and Brent rose 2.85%.
bullets: WHAT MOVED. The 04-Aug official settled cash $3,271.00 (+$11.00, +0.34%), 3M $3,236.50 (+$24.50, +0.76%), stock 260,900 t (-1,750 t, 25th straight draw, -48.8% year-to-date). The forward outran the prompt for the first time in this leg, and the cash-3M backwardation NARROWED to +$34.50 from +$48.00 - so the spread and the flat price moved in OPPOSITE directions on the session, which is worth stating plainly rather than smoothing.

WHY IT MATTERS. The premise of the previous session reversed inside two days. The claimed reopening of the Strait of Hormuz was publicly denied by Tehran, which said it was talking only to Oman about a routing; Washington accused Iran's leadership of duplicity; a cargo ship reported being struck near the strait's Omani coast; Brent rose about 2.85% to roughly $86. Aluminium is therefore no longer rising in defiance of the headline - it is rising with it, which is a weaker version of the tightness argument because it re-attaches part of the price to something reversible.

WHAT THE CURVE IS SAYING. A prompt premium that narrows while the 3-month outruns cash is the market pricing DURATION, not intensity: buyers paying up further out the curve are lengthening their estimate of how long the corridor stays impaired, rather than scrambling for metal today. Two facts sit under that: exchange cover is roughly two days of world consumption, and the first full-quarter Gulf producer P&L confirmed the curtailment is still running rather than restarting.

WHAT TO WATCH. Today's 13:20-London official - whether the backwardation narrows a second time and whether stock breaks 260,000 t, now 900 t away; published Hormuz transit counts, which are the only test of whether either version of the diplomacy is real; Century's Q2 tomorrow and Hindalco's Q1 FY27 on Friday for the US-tariff and Indian-cost reads; and the mid-August anode, CPC and coal-tar-pitch settlement cycle now that the crude relief has reversed.

kpis.label: Cash-3M spread
kpis.note: BACKWARDATION (cash ABOVE 3M) at +$34.50 on the 04-Aug official, NARROWER than 03-Aug's +$48.00 by $13.50. Convention: cash > 3M = backwardation = nearby tightness; cash < 3M = contango. EXPLICIT CALL-OUT - THE SPREAD AND THE FLAT PRICE MOVED IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS ON THIS SESSION: both price legs rose while the prompt premium fell. That is a different signal from Monday's and it is the honest one to report. Read plainly, the bid moved OUT the curve: buyers paid up more for forward metal (3M +0.76%) than for prompt metal (cash +0.34%), which is the signature of pricing a LONGER disruption rather than an acute nearby squeeze. It is not a tightness failure - +$34.50 remains a wide backwardation, double the +$17.00 of 31-Jul and in line with the late-July run - but it removes the 'new local high' claim the prior compile made, and a second consecutive narrowing would carry more information than this single session does.

lme.commentary: THE PRICE ROSE AGAIN, BUT FOR THE OPPOSITE REASON. Cash settled $3,271.00 on 04-Aug, +$11.00 (+0.34%), and 3M $3,236.50, +$24.50 (+0.76%) - a second consecutive higher official and the highest cash since early June, with stock drawing a 25th straight session to 260,900 t. The prior compile read Monday's 2% rise as the market voting 'physical' against a de-escalation headline; that headline did not survive 48 hours. Tehran denied that bilateral talks had resumed, saying it was speaking only to Oman and only about a new Hormuz route; Trump publicly called Iranian leadership 'unbelievably duplicitous'; UKMTO reported another cargo vessel struck near the strait's Omani coast; and Brent, which had fallen 4.61% on Monday, rose about 2.85% to roughly $86.16. So aluminium is once again moving WITH the geopolitical tape rather than in defiance of it. THE CURVE CARRIES THE MORE INTERESTING INFORMATION. For the first time in this advance the 3-month outran cash - +0.76% against +0.34% - and the cash-3M backwardation NARROWED to +$34.50 from Monday's +$48.00. Spread and flat price therefore moved in OPPOSITE directions, and that is a materially different message from Monday's. Read plainly, the bid moved out the curve: buyers paid up more for forward metal than for prompt metal, which is the signature of pricing a LONGER disruption rather than an acute nearby squeeze. It does not break the tightness case - +$34.50 is double the +$17.00 of 31-Jul and sits alongside a 25th consecutive draw - but it does retire the 'new local high' claim made one session ago, and a second narrowing would carry more weight than this one. WHAT DID NOT CHANGE IS THE WAREHOUSE. Stock at 260,900 t is another century low on records back to January 1998, -48.77% year-to-date from 509,250 t on 02-Jan, with the draw running an almost mechanical 1,500-1,750 t per session for three weeks. Total exchange cover is roughly two days of global consumption. The 260,000 t level breaks on the next report at that rate, which is why the stock axis was re-bracketed down to 250,000 t on this run rather than after the break. Neither Monday's de-escalation headline nor Tuesday's re-escalation has touched this series, and the first BUILD - not any further draw - remains the single most informative thing that could happen to it. SOURCING DISCIPLINE: the 04-Aug board was taken from Westmetall's German overview page, cache-busted, after the English overview was again found serving a stale snapshot - this time 03-Aug. That is the third occurrence of the documented cache failure mode in a week, and it was caught the same way each time: cross-checking the two language versions and confirming that all six metals, the stock table and the FX fixings roll together onto one session, then verifying against the per-metal daily tables.

Talks are expected to open around late August. THE NEGOTIATING BACKDROP SWUNG BACK TOWARD SELLERS THIS RUN, HAVING SWUNG TO BUYERS LAST RUN. The de-escalation that undercut the scarcity narrative on 02-Aug was publicly disputed within 48 hours: Tehran denied bilateral talks had resumed and said it was speaking only to Oman about a Hormuz routing, Trump called Iran's leadership 'unbelievably duplicitous', and a cargo vessel reported being struck near the Omani coast of the strait with traffic still a trickle of peacetime flow. FOR THE SELLERS, the physical evidence also strengthened: exchange stock is at a century low of 260,900 t after 25 consecutive draws, EGA had 89 of 1,262 pots running at 02-Jul, and Alba's 04-Aug Q2 disclosure confirms it is still running 'disciplined production curtailments' with Lines 1-3 (19% of 1,623,000 t/y) offline since 15-Mar. FOR THE BUYERS, what survives is the firmer yen after the first joint US-Japan intervention since 2011, a Chinese downstream in its seasonal off-peak, and a prompt backwardation that narrowed to +$34.50 on 04-Aug.

Against the 04-Aug cash official of $3,271.00 an all-in Japanese delivered equivalent computes to roughly $3,641/t, of which the premium is about 10.2% - the premium share fell purely because the metal price rose, not because the premium moved. THE FX LEG REMAINS THE LIVE VARIABLE: USD/JPY sits near 157.8 after Japan's Ministry of Finance and the US Treasury confirmed a coordinated yen-buying intervention on 03-Aug, the first joint action since 2011, with Tokyo warning it stands ready to act again. The yen has given back part of its post-intervention gain as the dollar firmed on the Fed's hawkish tilt, which partially reverses the affordability improvement Japanese buyers banked on Monday.

Billet premiums carry the duty-paid structure plus the conversion spread over P1020, so they move with both metal availability and extruder order books, and European extrusion demand remains the soft spot in the regional balance. PERIODIC ASSESSMENT - premium assessments do not re-price daily. This row is carried at its own assessment date and is NOT a current-session value; no daily move should be inferred from it. The US premium is overwhelmingly a TARIFF construct rather than a scarcity signal: at the 04-Aug cash official of $3,271.00 the 50% Section 232 rate on aluminium articles is $1,635.50/t on its own, up $5.50 from Monday's $1,630.00 purely because the metal price rose. THE RATE WAS RE-VERIFIED UNCHANGED THIS RUN and the direction of policy travel is toward WIDER coverage, not a lower rate: the US Department of Commerce published a Federal Register notice soliciting public comment on bringing 14 further derivative products - including aluminium powder, welder parts and tank semi-trailers - inside the Section 232 scope, with the 50% headline rate maintained. The 20-Jul-2026 proclamation allowing companies with an approved plan to build or expand a US primary smelter (construction beginning by 20-Jan-2029) to import at HALF the applicable rate against expected output remains the main identified route to compression, and no CBP implementing guidance has been issued yet.

This row is carried at its own assessment date and is NOT a current-session value; no daily move should be inferred from it. DECOMPOSITION REFRESHED EVERY RUN: at the 04-Aug cash official of $3,271.00 the 50% Section 232 ad-valorem leg alone is $1,635.50/t (up from $1,630.00 at the 03-Aug cash of $3,260.00), leaving roughly $744.50/t as the residual physical and logistics component against the carried $2,380/t assessment - about 68.7% tariff, 31.3% market. Derivative aluminium content pays 25%. Annex I-C reduced-rate carve-outs (15% all-in for Japan, Korea, the UK, Switzerland, Taiwan and EU members) run from 08-Jun-2026 to 31-Dec-2027 under Federal Register 2026-11314. Alcoa's Q2-2026 disclosure of roughly $35m of additional Section 232 cost on Canadian metal remains the clearest public evidence that the tariff is a real cash cost to cross-border producers as well as a premium inflator.

drivers.text: THE DE-ESCALATION PREMISE COLLAPSED WITHIN 48 HOURS: Tehran denied that bilateral talks had resumed, Trump called Iranian leadership 'unbelievably duplicitous', and another cargo ship was struck in the Strait of Hormuz with traffic still a trickle of peacetime flow — NBC News and the Washington Times both carry the 04-Aug account: Trump says talks to reopen the Strait of Hormuz are happening now; Tehran flatly denies it, saying it is talking only to Oman and only about a new Hormuz route. UKMTO reported a further attack on a cargo vessel near the strait's Omani coast, and Brent rose again - about +2.7% on the Washington Times account, +2.85% to roughly $86.16 on the Trading Economics tape. CNN carries Trump's 'unbelievably duplicitous' remark from 02-03 Aug after Tehran's denial. THIS DIRECTLY REVERSES THE PREMISE OF THE PRIOR COMPILE, which was built on a cancelled strike, agreed 'deal perimeters' and talks starting Monday afternoon. The premium complex has a Gulf-risk component in every regional row, and that component has been reinstated rather than removed. SMM's own 04-Aug comment is more measured and is reported here alongside: indirect technical talks made progress on fund repatriation and strait security, the geopolitical risk premium continued to narrow, but disputes over management of the strait persist and the resumption of navigation remains uncertain.
drivers.source: NBC News - Trump and Iran clash over Hormuz talks as another cargo ship is attacked (04-Aug-2026)

drivers.text: ALBA'S Q2 RESULTS, PUBLISHED 04-AUG, ARE THE FIRST FULL-QUARTER GULF-DISRUPTION P&L AND THEY CONFIRM THE CURTAILMENT IS STILL RUNNING: profit $172.5m (+164% y/y) and EBITDA $295m earned through 'disciplined production curtailments' rather than despite them — Aluminium Bahrain disclosed Q2-2026 profit attributable to equity holders of BHD 64.9m ($172.5m) against BHD 24.6m ($65.4m) a year earlier, +164% year-on-year, with EPS of 46 fils versus 17 fils and total comprehensive income BHD 64.5m (+195% y/y). H1-2026 profit is BHD 140.2m ($372.8m), +228% year-on-year against BHD 42.7m ($113.5m). Q2 EBITDA was $295m. The company attributes the outcome to disciplined production curtailments and rigorous management of raw-material flows amid unprecedented supply-chain challenges - which is the point for the premium complex: Reduction Lines 1, 2 and 3, roughly 19% of a 1,623,000 t/y smelter shut since 15-Mar-2026 on Hormuz transit disruption, are still out, and the company is earning record margins on a smaller book rather than restarting. Physical Gulf supply is not returning on a headline in either direction; the potlines are a months-long capital exercise. Alba held its results call on 05-Aug.
drivers.source: Aluminium Bahrain (Alba) - Q2 and H1-2026 financial results (04-Aug-2026)

drivers.text: Gulf war-risk cover at 3-10% of hull value - over $7 million per transit on a $100m vessel versus 0.25% pre-war - reprices on underwriters' cycles against realised losses, and the realised losses keep arriving — AL Circle's 24-Jul Middle East review assembles the public picture: war-risk insurance for Gulf transits stood at roughly 0.25% of hull value before February's escalation, quadrupled within three weeks of the first strikes, and by mid-July was quoted at 3-10% - the difference between a $250,000 premium and one exceeding $7 million on a single transit. Around 90% of ocean-going tonnage covered by the International Group of P&I Clubs faces cancellation-and-repricing clauses on short notice. The five GCC smelters produced about 6.16 Mt in 2025 (roughly 8% of world supply) with more than 80% exported; analysts pencil in 3-3.5 Mt of losses through 2026, near 5% of global primary supply. THE LOSS RECORD EXTENDED AGAIN THIS RUN: after the 01-Aug tanker strike near Lima, Oman and a second incident north-east of Khasab, a further cargo vessel reported being struck near the strait's Omani coast on 04-Aug. Insurance is a lagging, contractual cost; it did not fall on Monday's announcement of talks and it will not fall on Tuesday's denial of them either - but each new incident resets the underwriters' loss experience upward.
drivers.source: AL Circle - 2026 Middle East aluminium outlook: 5% of global supply, USD 7 million insurance and the Hormuz effect (24-Jul-2026)

drivers.text: US Section 232 at 50% is $1,635.50/t of the US duty-paid premium at the 04-Aug cash - re-verified unchanged this run, and Commerce is now consulting on pulling 14 MORE derivative products inside the scope — Aluminium articles made entirely or almost entirely of aluminium pay 50% ad valorem on full customs value; derivative aluminium content pays 25%. The structure originates in the April-2026 proclamation and was adjusted by the 01-Jun-2026 proclamation (Federal Register 2026-11314, effective 08-Jun-2026), whose 08-Jun-2026 to 31-Dec-2027 window applies to the Annex I-C reduced-rate carve-outs - 15% all-in for Japan, Korea, the UK, Switzerland, Taiwan and EU members. A 20-Jul-2026 proclamation additionally lets companies with an approved plan to build or expand a US primary smelter (construction beginning by 20-Jan-2029) import at half the applicable rate against expected output; no CBP guidance has been issued yet. NEW THIS RUN: the US Department of Commerce published a Federal Register notice soliciting public comments on including 14 additional derivative products - among them aluminium powder, welder parts and tank semi-trailers - within the Section 232 scope for steel, aluminium and copper, with the 50% headline rate maintained. MECHANICS: at the 04-Aug cash of $3,271.00 the 50% leg computes to $1,635.50/t exactly, up $5.50 from the 03-Aug cash of $3,260.00 purely through the metal price. This is why the US premium is not a clean scarcity signal and must not be read alongside MJP or EDU as if it were.
drivers.source: SMM / Federal Register - US seeks public comments on expanding metal tariffs to include 14 more products (05-Aug-2026)

Against that, oversupply remains structural: Guinea shipped a RECORD 114.8 Mt in H1-2026, +15% y/y, and China's alumina imports ran +749% y/y to 2.28 Mt in H1 with 91.7% of it Australian. SMM's 02-Aug inventory note recorded bauxite stocks at ten Chinese ports falling 730,000 mt week-on-week as at 31-Jul, the first materially tighter port read of the cycle; the 04-Aug brief adds that ALUMINA port inventory continued to BUILD on high overseas arrivals. Its three-refinery Western Australian system - Pinjarra, Wagerup and Kwinana Beach - is the world's largest single alumina source at roughly 8% of the global market, so a 200-300 kt cut is a material trim to the ex-China balance even against a modelled surplus.

COMMERCIAL LOGIC OF A CHEAP-ALUMINA REGIME: low alumina is a principal reason the July earnings season was uniformly strong across the producer set - Alcoa's Aluminum segment posted record EBITDA at a 32.3% margin, Hydro beat on adjusted EBITDA, and Alba's 04-Aug Q2 disclosure showed $295m EBITDA and profit up 164% year-on-year while running curtailed. It is also why a falling metal price would not immediately translate into supply discipline. Chinese operating capacity is 45.31 Mt/y against a 45 Mt ceiling with H1 output of 22.34 Mt (+2.24% y/y); with alumina near its cost floor there is no cost-side mechanism forcing that capacity out. Watch the SHFE alumina contract's behaviour around 2,600-2,650 yuan/mt and, per SMM, the implementation or otherwise of Guinea's bauxite quota policy - the single identified route out of the surplus.

logistics.label: Strait of Hormuz transit
logistics.note: THE 48-HOUR REVERSAL IS THE STORY. Monday's board was built on a cancelled US strike, claimed 'deal perimeters' and an asserted immediate reopening of the strait. Reporting describes traffic through the bottleneck as still 'a trickle of its peacetime flow' against more than 100 commodity vessels daily before the war began on 28-February. SMM's own 04-Aug comment is more measured and is carried alongside: indirect technical talks progressed on fund repatriation and strait security with nuclear consultations about to begin, the geopolitical risk premium continued to narrow, but disputes over management of the strait persist and the resumption of navigation remains uncertain. logistics.label: Gulf war-risk insurance

Around 90% of ocean-going tonnage covered by the International Group of P&I Clubs faces cancellation-and-repricing clauses on short notice. THIS IS THE SLOWEST-MOVING PART OF THE DELIVERED-COST STACK AND IT MOVES ONLY ON REALISED LOSSES - which is why it did not fall on Monday's announcement of talks and has not risen on Tuesday's denial of them, but why each new incident resets the underwriters' loss experience upward. The loss record extended again this run with a cargo vessel reported struck near the strait's Omani coast on 04-Aug, after the 01-Aug tanker strike near Lima, Oman and a second incident north-east of Khasab. Even on a signed agreement, the insurance wedge is likely to persist for months, putting a floor under Gulf-origin delivered costs independent of the LME price.

headlines.title: A SECOND CONSECUTIVE HIGHER OFFICIAL, LED BY THE CURVE. Aluminium Bahrain reported Q2-2026 profit of BHD 64.9m ($172.5m), +164% year-on-year, EBITDA $295m, and H1 profit of BHD 140.2m ($372.8m), +228% - earned, in the company's own words, through 'disciplined production curtailments and rigorous management of raw material flows'. The Department of Commerce published a Federal Register notice seeking public comment on bringing 14 further derivative products - including aluminium powder, welder parts and tank semi-trailers - inside the Section 232 scope for steel, aluminium and copper, with the 50% headline rate maintained. Bullish for the US Midwest premium and for domestic producers; bearish for US downstream converters and for exporters into the US, and it further widens the gap between US delivered prices and the rest of the world.

THE ENERGY RELIEF LASTED ONE SESSION. Brent rose about 2.85% to roughly $86.16 after Monday's 4.61% fall, and Dutch TTF gas about 4.30% to roughly EUR 59.98/MWh after a 4.23% fall. The crude-to-green-coke-to-CPC-to-anode chain that was about to deliver August relief is no longer pointing that way, and the mid-August settlement cycle for green petcoke, CPC, coal tar pitch and prebaked anodes is the next hard read. Bearish for smelter margins, and it removes the improvement in European restart economics flagged one session ago.

OUTSIDE-CHINA OUTPUT FELL 6.7% YEAR-ON-YEAR IN JULY on reduced operating rates at several Middle Eastern smelters, per public market commentary, while China's 45 Mt production cap is expected to become more binding through the year. Set against that, the restart pipeline is real and dated: Slovalco in Slovakia from Q4-2026, the Missouri smelter by year-end, and EGA continuing to restore production at Al Taweelah. The balance question for 2027 is whether those restarts land before Gulf output normalises.

THE DOLLAR FIRMED ON A HAWKISH FED TILT. SMM attributes part of Tuesday's cross-market pressure on non-ferrous prices to a hawkish Fed pivot lifting the dollar index, which printed about 100.02 (+0.12%). The LME EUR/USD fixing eased to 1.15170 from 1.15330 and USD/JPY firmed to about 157.8, giving back part of the post-intervention yen gain. A firmer dollar is mechanically negative for dollar-denominated metals and, for Japanese buyers, partly reverses Monday's affordability improvement ahead of late-August Q4 premium talks.

catalysts.text: TODAY'S LME OFFICIAL, 13:20 London. Three reads: (1) does the cash-3M backwardation narrow a SECOND consecutive session from +$34.50, which would matter far more than the first; (2) does the 3M hold above $3,212.00 and keep closing on the $3,303 measured 1.0x target; (3) does stock break 260,000 t - it is 900 t away at a prevailing draw rate of 1,500-1,750 t per session.

ALBA Q2 AND H1-2026 RESULTS CALL, 12:00 Bahrain time. The numbers are already public - profit $172.5m (+164% y/y), EBITDA $295m, H1 profit $372.8m (+228%) - so the call is about guidance: any restart timetable for Reduction Lines 1-3 (about 19% of 1,623,000 t/y, shut since 15-Mar), the raw-material sourcing workaround, and the first commentary on Aluminium Dunkerque consolidation.

PUBLISHED HORMUZ AND BAB AL MANDEB TRANSIT COUNTS - the only observable that settles the contradiction between Washington's account of live talks and Tehran's denial. Hormuz traffic is still described as a trickle of peacetime flow against more than 100 commodity vessels daily pre-war; no count has been published for 02-04 Aug. A recovery toward pre-war levels is the single most bearish development possible for the premium complex.

WHETHER LME STOCK BREAKS 260,000 t - the draw has run 25 consecutive published sessions to 260,900 t, -48.77% year-to-date, at an almost mechanical 1,500-1,750 t per session. The threshold breaks on the next report at that rate. The first BUILD would be far more significant than any further draw: it would mean metal returning to warehouse, and combined with a second spread narrowing it would be the clearest turn signal available.

CENTURY ALUMINUM Q2-2026 RESULTS (after US close) - the purest US and Section-232 read in the peer set, and the cleanest test of how much of the roughly $2,380/t US Midwest duty-paid premium is converting into margin with Mt. Holly back at full capacity for the first time since 2015. Sharpened this run by Commerce's consultation on adding 14 more derivative products to the Section 232 scope.

HINDALCO Q1 FY27 RESULTS - management has guided to roughly 5% higher aluminium costs, so the read is whether Indian integrated economics hold now that the energy leg has re-inflated. India is the swing consumer the bull case relies on outside China, and Hindalco's upstream EBITDA strip has risen four consecutive quarters.

SMM WEEKLY CHINA ALUMINIUM INGOT AND BILLET SOCIAL INVENTORY - the direct test of whether the sub-1 Mt destocking (953,000 t at 30-Jul, -35% from the early-May high) continues into the seasonal off-peak, with bar processing fees already down nearly 20% and extruder rates falling.

THE ANODE, CPC AND COAL-TAR-PITCH SETTLEMENT CYCLE, priced around the 17th-18th - the first hard evidence of whether the July crude spike or Monday's brief relief dominates the carbon leg. Now that Brent has reversed back to roughly $86, the expectation of August relief flagged one session ago looks unlikely to be met, and this is where it will show.

THE SHFE ALUMINA CONTRACT AROUND 2,600-2,650 YUAN/MT and any move on GUINEA'S BAUXITE QUOTA POLICY - SMM's 04-Aug brief states explicitly that before that policy is implemented the market lacks clear bullish alumina drivers. The 2609 contract settled 2,641 against an SMM-stated industry cost floor near 2,530, and SMM expects Chinese inventory to shift from weak destocking to slight buildup next week.

Q4-2026 MJP CIF JAPAN PREMIUM NEGOTIATIONS expected to open - Q3 settled at an 11-year high of $395/t on 06-Jul. The backdrop swung back toward sellers this run: the de-escalation was disputed, stock hit another century low and Alba confirmed sustained curtailments. Buyers retain a firmer yen and a narrower prompt backwardation. Scenario range carried here: $325-420, a construct rather than an assessment.

CHINA AUGUST PMIs AND INDUSTRIAL OUTPUT - whether July's split (private RatingDog 50.9 versus official NBS 49.2) resolves upward or downward - then the 15-16 September FOMC with dots, now more consequential after the Fed's hawkish tilt lifted the dollar index back above 100.

risks.text: A VERIFIED DIPLOMATIC BREAKTHROUGH REMAINS THE LARGEST SINGLE RISK BUT ITS ODDS FELL THIS RUN - the 02-Aug de-escalation was publicly disputed within 48 hours: Tehran denied that bilateral talks had resumed, saying it was speaking only to Oman about a Hormuz routing; Trump called Iranian leadership 'unbelievably duplicitous'; another cargo vessel was reported struck near the strait's Omani coast; and Brent rose about 2.85%. SMM's parallel read is more constructive - indirect technical talks progressing on fund repatriation and strait security with nuclear consultations about to begin - so the two credible public accounts diverge. The June precedent stands on the official record: on the 17-Jun ceasefire the official cash fell from $3,855.00 to $3,061.50, -20.6%. Deferred, not removed.

THE PROMPT PREMIUM NARROWED WHILE THE FLAT PRICE ROSE, AND THAT COMBINATION IS THE ONE TO WATCH - the cash-3M backwardation fell to +$34.50 from +$48.00 on the 04-Aug official, giving back a third of Monday's widening in a single session, with the 3-month outrunning cash for the first time in this advance. The level is still wide and sits alongside a 25th consecutive stock draw, so nearby tightness has not broken. But the prior compile treated the +$48.00 rebuild as the decisive proof of physical scarcity, and one session later a third of it is gone. A SECOND consecutive narrowing, especially alongside the first exchange stock build in 25 sessions, would mark the turn.

SUPPLY IS RETURNING WITHOUT A DEAL AND WOULD ACCELERATE WITH ONE - outside-China daily-average output rose 1.6% month-on-month in July on Middle East and Iceland restarts even as the year-on-year comparison fell 6.7%, and the dated pipeline is real: Slovalco +75 kt from Q4-2026, the Missouri smelter by year-end, Century's Mt. Holly already back at full capacity for the first time since 2015, Marston +75 kt, Balco 168 kt (+17% y/y), and EGA still restoring Al Taweelah. Chinese operating capacity is 45.31 Mt/y against the 45 Mt cap with H1 output 22.34 Mt (+2.24% y/y) and an industry margin of 6,999 yuan/mt (+56.8% y/y) that removes any incentive for restraint.

THE COST FLOOR STOPPED FALLING - AND THAT REMOVES A BEARISH ARGUMENT RATHER THAN ADDING ONE. Brent rose about 2.85% to roughly $86.16 and Dutch TTF about 4.30% to roughly EUR 59.98/MWh on 04-Aug, more than reversing Monday's falls, so the crude-to-green-coke-to-CPC-to-anode chain is re-inflating rather than delivering the August relief flagged one session ago. Chinese alumina meanwhile stayed flat at 2,641 yuan/mt on the SHFE, about 4.4% above SMM's stated 2,530 yuan/mt industry cost floor. The cost curve has SPLIT: carbon and power up, alumina flat. The prior run's concern - that a falling cost curve would protect margins on the way down and prevent supply discipline - has partly reversed.

CHINESE DOWNSTREAM DEMAND REMAINS THE WEAK LINK - aluminium bar processing fees are down nearly 20% as orders dry up in the seasonal off-peak, extruder operating rates are falling, and SMM attributes the ingot destocking to 953,000 t to supply contraction and a rising liquid-aluminium share rather than to demand pull. SMM's 04-Aug commentary explicitly cites weak traditional end-use demand in the Chinese off-season alongside continued rollout of long-term capacity outside China. The official NBS manufacturing PMI is in contraction at 49.2 with non-manufacturing at 49.0.

THE Q4 MJP PREMIUM NEGOTIATION IS NOW GENUINELY TWO-SIDED - sellers regained ground this run as the de-escalation was disputed, exchange stock hit another century low and Alba confirmed sustained curtailments, but buyers still hold a yen materially firmer than a week ago after the first joint US-Japan intervention since 2011, a prompt backwardation that narrowed to +$34.50, and a soft Chinese downstream. USD/JPY gave back part of the intervention gain to about 157.8 as the dollar firmed. Talks are expected to open around late August off an 11-year-high $395/t Q3 settlement; the scenario range carried here is $325-420 and is a construct, not an assessment.

EXTERNAL DEMAND CONTINUES TO OUTPERFORM THE OFFICIAL CHINA SURVEY - the private RatingDog July manufacturing PMI printed 50.9, in expansion, against NBS 49.2, with new orders up a 14th consecutive month and foreign sales rising for the first time in three. Korea 53.1, Taiwan 55.1 and Vietnam 52.9 all expanded with export orders improving, and LME copper set a fresh 2026 high at $14,195.00 cash on 04-Aug with exchange stock drawing 5,675 t - the cleanest cross-metal contradiction of a demand-collapse read. This is a risk to the BEARISH case, not to the bullish one.

TIGHTENING RISK RE-ASSERTED ITSELF THIS RUN - SMM attributes part of Tuesday's pressure on non-ferrous prices explicitly to a hawkish Fed pivot lifting the dollar index back above 100. The Fed held 9-3 on 29-Jul with three dissents FOR a hike and the Bank of England 6-3 on 30-Jul. June US core PCE at +0.1% m/m and 3.3% y/y leans dovish, but the reversal in oil and gas puts the energy impulse back into the second-half inflation path, which works against the disinflation case. A firmer dollar is mechanically negative for dollar-denominated metals. Decision point: the 15-16 September FOMC with dots.
